[]{#id1}

# Search Handlers[¶](#search-handlers "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

The easy and intuative way of handling query/search requests.

::::::::::: {#search-handler-callback .section}
## Search Handler Callback[¶](#search-handler-callback "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

[[async]{.pre} [def]{.pre} [search_handler_callback(query)]{.pre}]{.sig-name .descname}

: This is an scheme of a basic search handler callback that returns
  items.

  See the [[registering search handlers section]{.std
  .std-ref}](#register-search-handler){.reference .internal} for
  information on how to register your search handler.

  flogin will attemp to convert whatever the callback returns into a
  list of results. If a dictionary is given, flogin will try and convert
  it into an [[`Result`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
  .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result "flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result"){.reference
  .internal} via [[`from_dict()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
  .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result.from_dict "flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result.from_dict"){.reference
  .internal}

  The callback can also be an async iterator, and yield the results.

  Parameters[:]{.colon}

  : **query** ([[`Query`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.query.Query "flogin.query.Query"){.reference
    .internal}) -- The query data

  Return type[:]{.colon}

  : [[`Result`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result "flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result"){.reference
    .internal} \| list\[[[`Result`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils
    .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result "flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result"){.reference
    .internal}\] \| dict \| str \| int \| Any

  Yields[:]{.colon}

  : [[`Result`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result "flogin.jsonrpc.results.Result"){.reference
    .internal} \| dict \| str \| int \| Any

  Returns[:]{.colon}

  : flogin will take the output in whatever form it is in, and try its
    best to convert it into a list of results. Worst case, it casts the
    item to a string and handles it accordingly.

:::: {.highlight-py .notranslate}
::: highlight
    # Return a string, which gets turned into a result
    async def search_handler_callback_example(query):
        return "This is a string"
    # flogin will return a single result to flow launcher, which will look something like this:
    # Result(title="This is a string")
:::
::::

:::: {.highlight-py .notranslate}
::: highlight
    # Return a list of strings, which gets turned into a list of strings
    async def search_handler_callback_example(query):
        return ["Foo", "Bar", "Apple", "Pear"]
    # flogin will return a list of results to flow launcher, which will look something like this:
    # [
    #   Result(title="Foo"),
    #   Result(title="Bar"),
    #   Result(title="Apple"),
    #   Result(title="Pear"),
    # ]
:::
::::

:::: {.highlight-py .notranslate}
::: highlight
    # Return an int, which gets casted to a string and turned into a result.
    async def search_handler_callback_example(query):
        return 25
    # flogin will return a single result to flow launcher, which will look something like this:
    # Result(title=str(25))
:::
::::

:::: {.highlight-py .notranslate}
::: highlight
    # yield a couple of numbers
    async def search_handler_callback_example(query):
        yield 2
        yield 3
        yield 25
        yield 30
    # flogin will return a list of results to flow launcher, which will look something like this:
    # [
    #   Result(title=str(2)),
    #   Result(title=str(3)),
    #   Result(title=str(25)),
    #   Result(title=str(30)),
    # ]
:::
::::
:::::::::::

:::: {#conditions .section}
## Conditions[¶](#conditions "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

flogin uses condition functions to determine which handler should be
used on a certain query. A condition function should take a single
parameter ([[`Query`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.query.Query "flogin.query.Query"){.reference
.internal}), and return a bool. [`True`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre} means the search handler that this condition is
associated with should be used on this query, and [`False`{.docutils
.literal .notranslate}]{.pre} means that the search handler shouldn't be
used on this query. See the [[builtin conditions section]{.std
.std-ref}](api.html#builtin-search-conditions){.reference .internal} of
this page's api reference for a list of builtin conditions.

::: {#condition-example .section}
[]{#id2}

### Condition Example[¶](#condition-example "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

[[def]{.pre} [condition(query)]{.pre}]{.sig-name .descname}

: This is called when flogin is determining if a certain query handler
  should be used for a certain query or not.

  Parameters[:]{.colon}

  : **query** ([[`Query`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.query.Query "flogin.query.Query"){.reference
    .internal}) -- The query that will be give to the search handler

  Return type[:]{.colon}

  : [[`bool`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool "(in Python v3.14)"){.reference
    .external}

  Returns[:]{.colon}

  : A bool. [`True`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} means the
    search handler that this condition is associated with should be used
    on this query, and [`False`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}
    means that the search handler shouldn't be used on this query.
:::
::::

:::::::::::: {#registering-handlers .section}
[]{#register-search-handler}

## Registering Handlers[¶](#registering-handlers "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

There are 3 main ways to register handlers:

1.  [[Using the plugin.search decorator]{.std
    .std-ref}](#register-search-handler-by-plugin-search-deco){.reference
    .internal}

2.  [[Using plugin.search as a classmethod]{.std
    .std-ref}](#register-search-handler-by-plugin-search-deco-classmethod){.reference
    .internal}

3.  [[Subclassing and registering your search handler]{.std
    .std-ref}](#subclass-and-register-search-handler){.reference
    .internal}

::::: {#plugin-search-decorator .section}
[]{#register-search-handler-by-plugin-search-deco}

### Plugin.search decorator[¶](#plugin-search-decorator "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

If you want to create a handler outside of your [[`Plugin`{.xref .py
.py-class .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.plugin.Plugin "flogin.plugin.Plugin"){.reference
.internal} class using a decorator, you can use the [[`search()`{.xref
.py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.plugin.Plugin.search "flogin.plugin.Plugin.search"){.reference
.internal} decorator.

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    @plugin.search()
    async def my_handler(query: Query):
        return f"Your query was: {query.text}"
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {#plugin-search-decorator-as-classmethod .section}
[]{#register-search-handler-by-plugin-search-deco-classmethod}

### Plugin.search decorator as classmethod[¶](#plugin-search-decorator-as-classmethod "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

The [[`search()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.plugin.Plugin.search "flogin.plugin.Plugin.search"){.reference
.internal} decorator can also be used as a classmethod to define search
handlers inside of a plugin class. Like so:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    class MyPlugin(Plugin):
        @Plugin.search()
        async def my_handler(self, query: Query):
            return f"Your query was: {query.text}"
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {#subclassing-and-registering-a-search-handler .section}
[]{#subclass-and-register-search-handler}

### Subclassing and registering a search handler[¶](#subclassing-and-registering-a-search-handler "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

Using the decorator isn't the only weay to create search handlers, you
can also subclass the [[`SearchHandler`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils
.literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.search_handler.SearchHandler "flogin.search_handler.SearchHandler"){.reference
.internal} object and register the handler.

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    class MyHandler(SearchHandler):
        def __init__(self) -> None:
            super().__init__(condition=PlainTextCondition("egg"))

        async def callback(self, query: Query):
            return "You found the easter egg!"
:::
::::
:::::
::::::::::::

::::::: {#error-handling .section}
## Error Handling[¶](#error-handling "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

flogin is callback focused, so callbacks are used to handle errors in
search handlers. If you are using the [[`search()`{.xref .py .py-func
.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.plugin.Plugin.search "flogin.plugin.Plugin.search"){.reference
.internal} decorator to make your handler, you can use the
[[`error()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.search_handler.SearchHandler.error "flogin.search_handler.SearchHandler.error"){.reference
.internal} decorator to register an error handler.

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    @plugin.search()
    async def my_handler(query: Query):
        ...

    @my_handler.error
    async def my_error_handler(error: Exception):
        return f"An error occured! {error!r}"
:::
::::

Alternatively, if you are subclassing your handler, you can override the
[[`on_error()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.search_handler.SearchHandler.on_error "flogin.search_handler.SearchHandler.on_error"){.reference
.internal} method to handle your error.

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    class MyHandler(SearchHandler):
        async def callback(self, query: Query):
            ...

        async def on_error(error: Exception):
            return f"An error occured! {error!r}"
:::
::::
:::::::

::::::::::::::::: {#caching .section}
## Caching[¶](#caching "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

If your results are predicable and don't change much, a great option is
to cache the results to make response times just that much faster.
Additionally, if web requests are involved, the
[`ignore_cancellation_requests`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}
parameter in [[`Plugin`{.xref .py .py-class .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.plugin.Plugin "flogin.plugin.Plugin"){.reference
.internal} combined with cached search handlers can help reduce the
amount of web requests that are made. For this, a [[caching module]{.std
.std-ref}](api.html#caching-reference){.reference .internal} is
provided. Here is a quick walkthrough:

There are 3 provided decorators:

1.  [[`cached_coro()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.caching.cached_coro "flogin.caching.cached_coro"){.reference
    .internal}

This decorator can be used to cache the result of coroutines.

2.  [[`cached_gen()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.caching.cached_gen "flogin.caching.cached_gen"){.reference
    .internal}

This decorator can be used for caching async generators.

3.  [[`cached_property()`{.xref .py .py-func .docutils .literal
    .notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.caching.cached_property "flogin.caching.cached_property"){.reference
    .internal}

This decorator ca be used for caching properties, almost exacly like
[functools.cached_property](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functools.html#functools.cached_property){.reference
.external}

::::::::: {#useage .section}
### Useage[¶](#useage "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

The useage of each decorator is the same. You can use them as-is, for
example:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    @cached_coro
    async def my_coro():
        ...
:::
::::

or you can call it:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    @cached_coro()
    async def my_coro():
        ...
:::
::::

If you call the decorator, you can pass an argument which acts as a
[`name`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} parameter. This
parameter is used in combination with [[`clear_cache()`{.xref .py
.py-func .docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.caching.clear_cache "flogin.caching.clear_cache"){.reference
.internal} to fully customize which cached items you want to clear. The
default [`name`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} value is
[`None`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}, but you can pass a
custom one, like so:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    @cached_coro("my_coro")
    async def my_coro():
        ...
:::
::::
:::::::::

::::::::: {#clearing-the-cache .section}
### Clearing the cache[¶](#clearing-the-cache "Link to this heading"){.headerlink}

To clear the cache, you can use [[`clear_cache()`{.xref .py .py-func
.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre}](api.html#flogin.caching.clear_cache "flogin.caching.clear_cache"){.reference
.internal}. See the above section about the [`name`{.docutils .literal
.notranslate}]{.pre} parameter for more information about where the
[`name`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre} comes from.

To clear the cache of every cached object, don't pass any parameters.
Example:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    clear_cache()
:::
::::

To clear the cache of every cached object that doesn't have a set name,
pass [`None`{.docutils .literal .notranslate}]{.pre}. Example:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    clear_cache(None)
:::
::::

Lastly, to clear the cache of a specific item, pass it's name. Example:

:::: {.highlight-default .notranslate}
::: highlight
    @cached_coro("my_coro")
    async def my_coro():
        ...

    # just clear the cache of 'my_coro' and nothing else
    clear_cache('my_coro')
:::
::::
:::::::::
:::::::::::::::::
